henry.title: Moon and Mars Field Notes
henry.mission: Drive on the Moon and on Mars, write what each place looks like, and use the reading to name one difference in their air.
henry.done: Both rows of the table are filled, and problems 2 and 3 are answered.
words: where the ground meets the sky

flow.title: Read, then look at both worlds
flow.teach:
NASA Space Place says the Moon has almost no atmosphere. It also says Mars has a very thin atmosphere made mostly of carbon dioxide, and people could not breathe it.

Air can change how a sky looks. Write the colors and shapes you see today.

Drive with W, A, S, and D. Stop and look. A grown-up switches from the Moon to Mars.
pics: W forward, A left, D right, S back. Stop often.

flow.title: One difference you saw
flow.teach: Look back at your two rows. Name one thing that was different. If they looked the same, write what was the same.

flow.title: Use the reading
flow.teach: Use the reading. The Moon has almost no air. Mars has thin air. Say that difference in your own words.
flow.sheet: In your own words, what is one difference in the air of the Moon and Mars?

henry.challenge:
Optional. NASA lists the Moon's pull as 1.62 and Mars's pull as 3.73. Round each to a whole number. About how many times as strong is the Mars number?

Space Place also says the Moon has about one-sixth of Earth's gravity. A 60-pound rock on Earth would weigh about 60 divided by 6 pounds on the Moon. What is that?
henry.adult:
Your setup time is not part of his 15 minutes. Open Regolith yourself. This page cannot start it. Press H and follow H if it disagrees with this page. Do not overwrite a save you want. Land on a readable Moon name, then a readable Mars name. Gale crater is a good Mars choice if you can read it. Other readable Mars names include Jezero crater and Meridiani Planum. He uses only W A S D. Pause his timer while you switch. Both boys can take a short turn on the same landing.

If a world will not appear, use the Space Place pages below and write photo by that row.

NASA Space Place, Moon: the Moon has almost no atmosphere and about one-sixth of Earth's gravity. NASA Space Place, Mars: a very thin atmosphere made mostly of carbon dioxide. NASA fact sheets: Moon surface gravity 1.62 m/s², Mars 3.73 m/s². The game's model pulls are about 1.62 and about 3.7. Those are not the same printed figures, and the screen has no gravity meter. Do not grade colors. Do not count craters as a fact about the whole world. Do not use jumps or top speed. Skip Titan, Io, and Europa.

Older pictures for you only:

Space Place: Moon · Space Place: Mars

parentKey.assess: Score the table, a difference taken from his own rows, and a sentence that the Moon has almost no air while Mars has thin air. Do not grade the colors or what he noticed. The challenge is not scored.

items.a: Both rows filled with the names you actually opened and what he saw. Any honest notes. Photo is fine if the game did not load.
A difference, or a sameness, that matches his table.
The Moon has almost no air. Mars has a thin atmosphere, mostly carbon dioxide. His own words are fine.
1.62 rounds to 2. 3.73 rounds to 4. 4 is about 2 times 2. Accept about 2 or a little more than 2. The 60-pound rock is about 10 pounds on the Moon (60 ÷ 6).
